subject: FQDN onboarding checkpoint: customer-managed zone provisioning & cert rotation roadmap
messages:

To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: FQDN onboarding checkpoint: customer-managed zone provisioning & cert rotation roadmap

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To keep momentum on the private deployment (VPC) onboarding, we need to align on two items before we schedule the network cutover window: zone provisioning (how ACME will delegate the customer-managed FQDN to Redwood) and the certificate lifecycle model for the private endpoints.

Quick asks:
- Can ACME create a delegated NS record for the subzone we requested (private-api.acme.internal) or do you prefer we issue glue records and host an authoritative subzone?
- Do you have an existing internal CA/HSM/KMS constraint (we saw notes about HSM-backed keys in your security questionnaire) that would prevent us from using ACME with short-lived certs?
- For mutual TLS: will your service mesh require client cert pinning for our outbound calls, or is one-way TLS with client IP allowlist acceptable for the first rollout?

I've attached a small zone provisioning template and a suggested rotation timeline for your infra team's review. If we get agreement on the three bullets above, we'll propose a 2-week onboarding plan with a single maintenance window for DNS delegation + cert swap.

Next steps (proposed):
1) ACME confirms NS delegation method + provides zone template back (we can accept a signed zone file or granting our delegated account).
2) Redwood publishes CSR proof instructions and a sample ACME workflow (if using ACME).
3) Align on cert rotation cadence (30 days preferred for production; we can support 90d if HSM constraints require it).

Appreciate a quick confirm by EOD Monday so we can lock dates.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Principal Product Manager — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 22 Jul 2028 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FQDN onboarding checkpoint: customer-managed zone provisioning & cert rotation roadmap

Mina —

Thanks — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- We prefer to manage the parent zone ourselves and delegate a child NS for the subzone (private-api.acme.internal). We will add the NS records, please send the target names for the delegated nameservers.
- We operate an HSM-backed PKI for internal services. That means we cannot hand over private CA keys; however, we can mint short-lived certs via an internal ACME endpoint if Redwood supports ACME v2 (with token-based validation).
- mTLS: for the initial rollout we'll require one-way TLS with strong client IP allowlisting. Our long-term plan is to enable mTLS, but that will be a second-phase change once service-to-service identity is onboarded internally.

Attached is our zone template (customer-facing fields redacted) and a compliance note about our HSM policy. We can be flexible on rotation cadence if Redwood provides automation hooks — 30 days is preferred.

Sara Jones
Senior Cloud Engineer, ACME Corp

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Sara Jones <sara.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Jul 2028 14:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FQDN onboarding checkpoint: customer-managed zone provisioning & cert rotation roadmap

Sara / Mina —

Thanks for the details, Sara. Few technical notes and a suggested implementation pattern from the infra side:

Implementation pattern (recommended):
- DNS: ACME creates NS records for the subzone (private-api.acme.internal) pointing to our delegated nameservers (ns1-rw.redwood.internal, ns2-rw.redwood.internal). We will provide the nameserver FQDNs and verify delegation via SOA checks.
- Split-horizon: Use a private resolver in the customer's VPC that forwards the subzone to our authoritative nameservers. This avoids leaking the private namespace to public resolvers.
- Certs: If you expose an internal ACME endpoint, we can use ACME v2 with DNS-01 or TLS-ALPN-01 (DNS-01 preferred for private zones). We propose short-lived certs (30d) rotated automatically; we will publish a webhook for rotation events or support a Pull CSR flow if you prefer to issue certs from your HSM.
- mTLS: For phase 1, Redwood will enforce one-way TLS termination on the edge container and optionally configure mutual-auth if ACME later provides client certs.

Operational checklist (what Redwood will do):
1) Provide delegated nameserver FQDNs and validate NS delegation.
2) Provide CSR proof instructions + sample ACME token exchange payload.
3) Schedule a 3-hour maintenance window for the final DNS delegation + cert swap.
4) Publish rotation webhook and a minimal runbook (https://redwoodai.app/ops/runbooks/fqdn-onboard).

Security notes: we will never request private CA keys. If ACME issues certs from its HSM, we will accept either an automated ACME push or a signed short-lived cert bundle over an SFTP endpoint — whichever matches your policy.

Jonas Weber
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

Week 0 (this week): confirm NS delegation method + ACME endpoint details from ACME infra
Week 1: test delegation in staging VPC, validate CSR + ACME token flow, provision initial certs
Week 2: schedule maintenance window (3 hours) to flip NS in prod and perform cert swap; rollback plan included

Please review and respond with any blockers. If ACME confirms the internal ACME endpoint and can accept our DNS-01 challenges, we'll target August 8th for the prod flip. I've opened a brief DocuSign to capture the SLA exception for the maintenance window (link below).
